deduped_items.title: Sibol nails maiden Asian Games esports medal with Pokemon Unite bronze
deduped_items.summary: The Sibol Pokemon Unite team of Lance David, Ducke Harnold Leoncio, Lawrence Anthony Gatmaitan, Kim Rey Salazar, Robert Jon Mempin, and Michael Vaughn Ocio earn the Philippines' first-ever esports medal in the Asian Games
deduped_items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines scored a breakthrough esports medal at the Asian Games as Sibol clinched a Pokemon Unite bronze at the Aichi Sky Expo in Japan on Sunday, September 27.
The team of Lance David, Ducke Harnold Leoncio, Lawrence Anthony Gatmaitan, Kim Rey Salazar, Robert Jon Mempin, and Michael Vaughn Ocio still secured a bronze despite a 2-0 loss to Indonesia in the semifinals.
Sibol built a commanding lead in the first game but ran out of steam, surrendering the opener and failing to recover as it fell to a sweep in the best-of-three affair.
Nevertheless, it was still a commendable result as the Philippines won its first-ever esports medal in the Asian Games, which included esports as a demonstration competition in 2018 then adopted it as a medal event in 2023.
“I’m still in awe because this is the first time and I’m really happy for the boys because this is something they’ll carry with them for the rest of their lives, that they were able to bring home a medal to the Philippines,” said Sibol head coach Albert Camp.
Sibol topped Group A with 4 points then scored a 2-0 win over Hong Kong in the quarterfinals to assure itself of a podium finish.
Another Sibol squad is guaranteed a medal as the Honor of Kings crew of Golden Hart Dajao, Justine Ritchie Tan, Charles Roman Esguerra, Dragon Hart Dajao, Jhon Mike Tungol, and Chammy Paul Nazarrea advanced to the semifinals following a 2-0 victory over South Korea.
Sibol battles China on Monday, September 28, for a spot in the gold-medal match. – Rappler.com

deduped_items.title: Bangkok floods force thousands into shelters
deduped_items.summary: BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
deduped_items.body_text:
BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
Nearly 4,900 people have been evacuated to shelters, with around 52,000 households affected by the floods, which prompted a disaster declaration across the capital, according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA).
More than 330 millimetres (13 inches) of rain fell in some areas of the city between Thursday and Sunday, the weather agency said.
Thailand is used to wet weather and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several Bangkok residents said this year seemed worse.
"Our house was underwater for about 30 hours," office worker Kosin Nilset, who lives along the Premprachakorn canal on the outskirts of the capital, told AFP on Sunday morning.
"This time, the water level is higher than the 2011 flood," the 44-year-old said.
Widespread deluges across the Southeast Asian country in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.
Kosin and his family lifted their belongings once they saw the water level was higher than the canal retaining wall, but their ground floor was still left soaked.
"At least tap water and electricity are working," Kosin said, as he used a broom to sweep out water.
Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos trudged through murky floodwaters in Bangkok's east -- knee-deep in some areas of a grocery store parking lot -- floating their belongings in plastic tubs alongside them, AFP journalists saw.
- 'Sleeping on the table' -
Water levels in Bangkok's network of canals remained high on Sunday morning, with authorities working to speed up drainage, the BMA said.
More rain was forecast throughout Sunday for Bangkok and its surrounding provinces, but would begin to taper off on Monday, it said.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as the planet continues to heat up because of fossil fuel emissions.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said several roads were still flooded and warned Bangkok residents in a Facebook Live post to avoid unnecessary travel.
Chadchart visited a temporary shelter on Saturday night in a school in the Kheha Romklao area, where he said about 1,000 people were evacuated.

deduped_items.title: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence
deduped_items.summary: The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said. It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or inte
deduped_items.body_text:
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province.
“The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or intelligence agencies in any internal clashes in Nuristan or elsewhere in Afghanistan, including allegations of recruiting or training former Afghan security personnel or facilitating Daesh or any other terrorist group operating in Afghanistan.”
The information ministry’s statement came after Afghanistan’s defence ministry alleged that Pakistan-backed individuals had crossed the border and were involved in the reported violence.
The information ministry pointed out that “not a shred of evidence has been produced to substantiate Pakistan’s involvement; no identities, documents, communications, forensic evidence or independent verification”.
It further noted that an alleged video “being peddled on social media to support this false claim only shows a few unarmed individuals who are not even properly dressed or equipped were arrested in what seems to be a pre-planned video shoot by Afghan Taliban regime, well known for lies and fabricated claims”.
“Instead of externalising responsibility for its internal security challenges through fanciful allegations, the Afghan Taliban regime should take credible and verifiable action against terrorist organisations operating from its territory and fulfil its commitments that Afghan soil will not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country.”
The statement further said it was “particularly ironic for the Afghan Taliban regime to accuse Pakistan of supporting terrorism while terrorist organisations operating from Afghanistan continue to pose a direct threat to Pakistan and regional security”.
The ministry highlighted that the presence and activities of “terrorist groups of all types inside Afghanistan are well documented”, including in successive reports of the United Nations and other neutral international organisations.
“Attempts to manufacture a Pakistani connection cannot obscure the reality that these terrorist groups continue to find sanctuary and [a] permissive environment for growth in Afghan territory,” it asserted.
“Such claims by this non-inclusive, non-representative Taliban regime are also reflective of lies to externalise internal dissent and oppression of women, children and minorities,” the ministry said.
Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.
According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afghan Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.
The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).
Pak-Afghan tensions
Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism. Meanwhile, September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.
Information Minister

deduped_items.title: US’ Taiwan policy unchanged: envoy
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            US’ Taiwan policy unchanged: envoy‘STATUS QUO’: ‘There’s no change in the Taiwan policy here,’ the US ambassador to China said, adding that the US is not changing its language or position on the issue
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 US policy toward Taiwan has not changed following talks between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平), Washington’s top envoy to Beijing said on Friday, a day after the two leaders met at the White House. “There’s no change in the Taiwan policy here,” US Ambassador to China David Perdue told CNBC in an interview aired on Friday morning when asked about the possibility that Xi might have tried to persuade Trump to soften his stance on Taiwan. Trump is “fully committed to the one China policy,” Perdue said, adding that the US remains committed to the Taiwan Relations Act, the Three Joint Communiques and the Six Assurances. US Ambassador to China David Perdue speaks during CNBC’s Squawk Box aired yesterday.Photo: Screen grab from CNBC Television’s YouTube channel “Nothing has changed there,” he said. “We’re not changing the language. We’re not changing our position there. We want peace across the [Taiwan] Strait. We don’t want coercion. We don’t support independence.” Perdue said Washington believed Xi had received that message, adding that Trump had “shown respect and listened to their side of that argument.” Taiwan was among the closely watched issues during Thursday’s Trump-Xi meeting, and the two leaders did not respond to reporters’ questions afterward on whether the issue had been discussed. According to the White House fact sheet on Xi’s visit, issued on Friday, the two leaders discussed bilateral trade and investment, geopolitical flashpoints, including Russia, North Korea and Iran, as well as drug control. Taiwan is notably absent from the White House fact sheet, unlike the readout published by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. According to China’s readout, Xi stressed China’s “clear cut” position on safeguarding “national reunification” and “territorial integrity.” “It is hoped that the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing Taiwan independence, and handle the Taiwan question with caution, so as to lay a solid foundation for China-US strategic cooperation and the development of bilateral relations,” the readout said. Trump has not publicly “opposed” Taiwanese independence, instead saying in May in an interview while visiting Beijing that he was not “looking to have somebody go independent” as he urged Beijing and Taipei to “cool down.” According to the White House fact sheet, the two leaders “recalled that United States and China were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war.” China’s readout does not mention the remark, but it was included in a report published by Xinhua on the same day. Taipei has rebuked that stance and accused Xi of distorting historical facts. The Mainland Affairs Council and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have stressed that it was the Republic of China, whose government relocated from China to Taiwan in 1949 after the Chinese Civil War, that fought alongside US forces in World War II. However, Taipei has not publicly responded to the White House’s fact sheet. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan (彭麗媛), on Friday concluded their three-day state visit to the US after having tea with Trump and US first lady Melania Trump at the White House and visiting the US National Archives. After Xi’s departure, Trump said on Truth Social that the meeting was one of “Friendship, Strength, and Success” for both countries. “We will be meeting again in November, in China, and then at the G20 in December, in Miami, Florida,” Trump wrote, adding that “much has been, and will be, accomplished.” The APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen in November. deduped_items.title: Allied nations call for Taiwan’s inclusion in UN
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Allied nations call for Taiwan’s inclusion in UNPLEA: How the UN addresses Taiwan’s security issue would be a test of its strength and relevance, Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine told the UN General Assembly
  - By Fion Khan / Staff writer, with CNA
 Only Taiwan’s elected government can represent the people of Taiwan, Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said on Friday at the UN General Assembly, calling for the nation’s inclusion in the UN. Taiwan and its 23 million people are a reality, and only its democratically elected government can represent it, Heine said when addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly General Debate. Appropriate ways must be found for Taiwan’s substantive participation in UN meetings if the UN is to be truly inclusive and effective in years to come, she said. Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine, bottom, addresses the 81st UN General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City on Friday.Photo: Reuters UN member states would experience pressure to accept a false narrative that UN Resolution 2758 serves as a legal pretext under the UN Charter for coercion or war, impairing freedom of navigation in one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, she said. Resolution 2758, passed in 1971, states that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is the only legitimate representative of China at the UN, which enabled Beijing to replace the Republic of China (ROC), Taiwan’s official name, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council. “Every nation in this hall may be told that aggression or coercion upon Taiwan is an internal matter somehow justified by an ancient UN seating chart resolution, a resolution which doesn’t even reference Taiwan,” she said. Tuvaluan Prime Minister Feleti Teo speaks during the 81st UN General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York on Friday.Photo: AP Appeasement never satisfies an aggressor’s wider agenda, and one taste is never enough, she said. UN member states might be told that “might makes right,” and that it is futile for small nations to resist a larger one, she said. “We will be asked, politely and impolitely, to turn a blind eye and look away,” she said, adding that how the UN addresses this very real security dilemma would be a test of its strength and relevance. Tuvaluan Prime Minister Feleti Teo also called for arrangements that enable the meaningful participation of the 23.5 million Taiwanese in the UN and related agencies. Taiwan has consistently demonstrated that it is an able, trustworthy and constructive partner in addressing global challenges, and its exclusion undermines the spirit and effectiveness of multilateral cooperation, he said. Tuvalu is gravely concerned by the escalating military activities around Taiwan, which threaten stability across the Strait, disrupt international transportation and trade, and jeopardize peace and security in the Pacific and beyond, he said. Tuvalu commends Taiwan for its calm and principled adherence to the values of the UN Charter, he said, urging all UN member states to uphold the same principles. The 81st session of the UN General Assembly opened on Sept. 8, with the general debate running from Tuesday last week to tomorrow. Three of Taiwan’s diplomatic allies — Paraguay, Eswatini and Palau — on Wednesday made a push for Taiwan’s inclusion in the UN.

deduped_items.title: US, China to open AI ‘communication channel’
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            US, China to open AI ‘communication channel’
  - AFP, WASHINGTON
 The US and China agreed to set up a “communication channel” for artificial intelligence (AI) incidents, the White House said on Friday, after a Washington summit short on breakthroughs. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) discussed matters ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the US. Xi’s visit to Washington was marked more by pomp than substance, but the White House said the nations agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents. US President Donald Trump, right, speaks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the steps of the US National Archives Museum in Washington on Friday.Photo: AP While billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, Xi took a more measured tone, saying that the technology must develop under human control. The White House also reported some deals from the visit, including China agreeing to import at least 10 million tonnes of coal from the US next year and in 2028. Additionally, the two countries agreed more favorable tariff treatment for US$30 billion of “non-sensitive goods” in each direction and two Chinese pandas were to arrive at a US zoo. Beijing did not immediately comment after the White House statements.

South African police probe mining feud shooting, 27 dead as elections near
Illegal miners live in the area, where powerful gangs control the illicit gold mining trade
South African police on Sunday were hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country’s problem with gun violence.
Officials were still establishing the motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town, but initial investigations suggested one could be a turf war between illegal miners and the other a business rivalry.
Violent crime remains rife in South Africa, despite government efforts to curb one of the highest per capita murder rates in the world.
In Wedela township, about 80 km (50 miles) from Johannesburg, 17 people were killed and 15 injured at a tavern when suspects armed with AK-47 rifles opened fire at around 9:30pm on Saturday, according to police.

deduped_items.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search
deduped_items.summary: Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silentGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastLoved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and
deduped_items.body_text:
Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.
He was last seen near the beginning of his trek across the Cordillera Huayhuash circuit, which is regarded as a challenging, high-altitude trek through the remote Andes mountains.
Regarded as a very experienced hiker by friends and family, the Melbourne man failed to make contact on Wednesday, his estimated return date.
He also failed to check back into the Krusty Hostel in Huaraz, where his luggage remains stored, and missed a scheduled flight from Lima to Cusco on Thursday.
“It’s really uncharacteristic of him to not have communicated at any point in his journey if he had the chance to,” longtime friend Kevin Nguyen said.
“It is a very popular trek, where you might have 200 to 300 hikers and guides per week during the busy season, so it is very uncharacteristic that no one’s seen him since day one or day two.”
The avid trekker misplaced a satellite beacon he was travelling with days before he set off on the 120km hike, raising further concerns.
Local mountain rescue organisation Socorro Andino Peruano has been hired by Yap’s family to help with the search.
His loved ones are holding out hope the rescue group, which recently rescued a Canadian trekker from the same trail, will be able to find him safe.
“Time is of the essence … because ultimately, as much as we were saying he’s been missing since the 23rd, he’s had no contact with anyone since the 14th,” Nguyen said.
Rescue crews completed their biggest day of search operations so far on Saturday (Sunday morning AEST), scouring various trails on the circuit to no avail.
“I know Jordan likes to orienteer and navigate and he’s quite an adventurer himself, so I wouldn’t be surprised if he tried an alternative route,” Nguyen said.
Yap had been planning the trek for more than a year and had recently bought a GPS watch to allow for offline maps to guide him on the hike.
“He was telling everyone about how he was ready to go on a big hike like this, (he was) really excited,” Nguyen said.
He was last known to be wearing a white jacket, green sunshade sweater and grey pants.
The experienced trekker was believed to be carrying a 40-litre hiking bag, Durston dome tent and hiking poles.
Family and friends are urging the Australian government to work with Peruvian officials and local authorities to mobilise further resources in and around the rugged region.
The Australian embassy in Peru is helping his family.
The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has been contacted for comment.

deduped_items.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search
deduped_items.summary: Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silentGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastLoved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and
deduped_items.body_text:
Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.
He was last seen near the beginning of his trek across the Cordillera Huayhuash circuit, which is regarded as a challenging, high-altitude trek through the remote Andes mountains.
Regarded as a very experienced hiker by friends and family, the Melbourne man failed to make contact on Wednesday, his estimated return date.
He also failed to check back into the Krusty Hostel in Huaraz, where his luggage remains stored, and missed a scheduled flight from Lima to Cusco on Thursday.
“It’s really uncharacteristic of him to not have communicated at any point in his journey if he had the chance to,” longtime friend Kevin Nguyen said.
“It is a very popular trek, where you might have 200 to 300 hikers and guides per week during the busy season, so it is very uncharacteristic that no one’s seen him since day one or day two.”
The avid trekker misplaced a satellite beacon he was travelling with days before he set off on the 120km hike, raising further concerns.
Local mountain rescue organisation Socorro Andino Peruano has been hired by Yap’s family to help with the search.
His loved ones are holding out hope the rescue group, which recently rescued a Canadian trekker from the same trail, will be able to find him safe.
“Time is of the essence … because ultimately, as much as we were saying he’s been missing since the 23rd, he’s had no contact with anyone since the 14th,” Nguyen said.
Rescue crews completed their biggest day of search operations so far on Saturday (Sunday morning AEST), scouring various trails on the circuit to no avail.
“I know Jordan likes to orienteer and navigate and he’s quite an adventurer himself, so I wouldn’t be surprised if he tried an alternative route,” Nguyen said.
Yap had been planning the trek for more than a year and had recently bought a GPS watch to allow for offline maps to guide him on the hike.
“He was telling everyone about how he was ready to go on a big hike like this, (he was) really excited,” Nguyen said.
He was last known to be wearing a white jacket, green sunshade sweater and grey pants.
The experienced trekker was believed to be carrying a 40-litre hiking bag, Durston dome tent and hiking poles.
Family and friends are urging the Australian government to work with Peruvian officials and local authorities to mobilise further resources in and around the rugged region.
The Australian embassy in Peru is helping his family.
The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has been contacted for comment.

deduped_items.body_text:
South African police probe mining feud shooting, 27 dead as elections near
Illegal miners live in the area, where powerful gangs control the illicit gold mining trade
South African police on Sunday were hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country’s problem with gun violence.
Officials were still establishing the motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town, but initial investigations suggested one could be a turf war between illegal miners and the other a business rivalry.
Violent crime remains rife in South Africa, despite government efforts to curb one of the highest per capita murder rates in the world.
In Wedela township, about 80 km (50 miles) from Johannesburg, 17 people were killed and 15 injured at a tavern when suspects armed with AK-47 rifles opened fire at around 9:30pm on Saturday, according to police.

deduped_items.title: La literatura del desplazamiento: las bestias nocturnas de Guillermo Arriaga
deduped_items.summary: Los siguientes libros del escritor Guillermo Arriaga (Ciudad de México, 1958) narran intensos viajes por la condición humana. deduped_items.title: Mora ilumina el debut de Rafa Márquez frente a Colombia
deduped_items.summary: El debut de Rafael Márquez al frente de la selección nacional tuvo el brillo de Gilberto Mora. El adolescente, quien recibió su diploma de bachillerato en Tijuana dos días después de deslumbrar en la Copa del Mundo, marcó el gol que rescató al equipo mexicano de una derrota frente a Colombia (1-1) en el estadio M&T Bank de Baltimore. El encuentro dejó una muestra de lo que será el proceso hacia 2030: liderazgos jóvenes, un estilo frontal basado en la secuencia de pases y el número 10 en las espa

deduped_items.title: Elena Poniatowska: Gabino Palomares
deduped_items.summary: Con su inseparable guitarra, a Gabino Palomares lo conocemos desde hace más de 50 años como cantautor y activista mexicano. Con su música ha recorrido toda la República al lado de luchadores sociales, reconocidos o anónimos, que defienden los ideales y derechos de los menos favorecidos. Con 76 años de vida y más de cinco décadas de componer música, Gabino ha escrito cientos de canciones y la que más gusta y enorgullece a los mexicanos es: La maldición de la Malinche. deduped_items.title: Qué vemos cuando miramos un animal: dos libros sobre la mirada, la carne y la condición humana
deduped_items.summary: Dos libros recientes convierten a los animales en una vía de entrada para pensar la condición humana. Kate Zambreno observa el cautiverio y las formas de mirar en Historias de animales, mientras Ieda Magri reconstruye en Una exposición el ritual rural de la faena.Entre la jaula y la carne aparecen preguntas sobre identidad, memoria, muerte y supervivencia.

deduped_items.title: How Rómulo Betancourt Allied with the US Without Surrendering Sovereignty
deduped_items.summary: In the 1960s, the Venezuelan president proved that democracy was a more sure bet for Washington's interests
deduped_items.body_text:
How Rómulo Betancourt Allied with the US Without Surrendering Sovereignty
In the 1960s, the Venezuelan president proved that democracy was a more sure bet for Washington's interests
John F. Kennedy receives Betancourt in the Oval Office on February 19, 1963. White House photograph by Abbie Rowe, JFK Presidential Library and Museum.
In 1898, the United States entered Cuba promising to liberate a nation; the subsequent occupation and the Platt Amendment ultimately granted it the right to intervene in the country’s affairs. A century before chavismo, Juan Vicente Gómez found a different formula: domestic order, foreign capital, and oil, all while leaving the citizenry out of the equation. Rafael Osío Cabrices and Marcus Golding have revisited both precedents to reflect on the Venezuela that would emerge after January 3. These two mirrors are uncomfortable, yet they are not the only ones; a third exists—also born of the relationship between Venezuela and the US—though it is based on a different idea of how to build stability.
During the 1950s, Venezuelan social democrat leader Rómulo Betancourt wrote from exile to convince Washington that its policy toward Latin America was based on a flawed premise. While military dictatorships might declare themselves anti-communist and guarantee a certain level of stability, repression, inequality, and a lack of civic participation paved the way for the very radicalization the US wished to contain. A democracy capable of enacting social reforms could serve as a more reliable ally.
This wasn’t Betancourt’s idea alone. Within the US government, there were already officials who viewed reformist forces as a more effective bulwark against communism. Betancourt’s own contribution lay elsewhere: articulating this argument from within Latin America and attempting to prove its validity while in power. Research by Steven Schwartzberg shows that this approach had begun even before the long exile triggered by the 1948 coup.
Upon returning to Venezuela after January 23, 1958, Betancourt did not ask the White House to build Venezuelan democracy. The major political parties agreed on rules for coexistence and the country held elections, which he won. His government undertook agrarian, educational, and social reforms starting in 1959, all while facing military conspiracies, guerrilla violence, and hostility from neighboring dictatorships. There were abuses, restrictions on civil liberties, and incomplete results. It was not a conflict-free democracy, but a democracy struggling to survive.
Both voting and finding a way out of the economic crisis remain priorities that oil alone cannot resolve.
That experience bolstered Betancourt’s argument before Washington. A State Department report from the time described Venezuela as a hemispheric leader in promoting social reform and economic development within a constitutional framework. This foreign alliance rested on a domestic political foundation: it did not rely solely on oil or on a shared stance against a common enemy.
The Cuban Revolution had made this discussion more urgent since January 1959. Upon arriving at the White House in 1961, John F. Kennedy understood that anti-communism alone was insufficient, and he found an exceptional partner in Betancourt. The Alliance for Progress sought to link development, social reform, and representative democracy. When Kennedy visited Venezuela in December 1961, the two governments issued a joint declaration framing economic cooperation within the context of “the effective practice of representative democracy.” Democracy was not a destination to be reached only when conditions became more favorable. It was an integral part of the journey itself.
1961 versus 2026
We can’t idealize that era. The Alliance for Progress yielded uneven results, and the US continued to tolerate dictatorships when it served its interests. Years later, Betancourt would welcome Jimmy Carter’s emphasis on human rights—as Guillermo Ramos Flamerich notes—

deduped_items.summary: In the 1960s, the Venezuelan president proved that democracy was a more sure bet for Washington's interests
deduped_items.body_text:
How Rómulo Betancourt Allied with the US Without Surrendering Sovereignty
In the 1960s, the Venezuelan president proved that democracy was a more sure bet for Washington's interests
John F. Kennedy receives Betancourt in the Oval Office on February 19, 1963. White House photograph by Abbie Rowe, JFK Presidential Library and Museum.
In 1898, the United States entered Cuba promising to liberate a nation; the subsequent occupation and the Platt Amendment ultimately granted it the right to intervene in the country’s affairs. A century before chavismo, Juan Vicente Gómez found a different formula: domestic order, foreign capital, and oil, all while leaving the citizenry out of the equation. Rafael Osío Cabrices and Marcus Golding have revisited both precedents to reflect on the Venezuela that would emerge after January 3. These two mirrors are uncomfortable, yet they are not the only ones; a third exists—also born of the relationship between Venezuela and the US—though it is based on a different idea of how to build stability.
During the 1950s, Venezuelan social democrat leader Rómulo Betancourt wrote from exile to convince Washington that its policy toward Latin America was based on a flawed premise. While military dictatorships might declare themselves anti-communist and guarantee a certain level of stability, repression, inequality, and a lack of civic participation paved the way for the very radicalization the US wished to contain. A democracy capable of enacting social reforms could serve as a more reliable ally.
This wasn’t Betancourt’s idea alone. Within the US government, there were already officials who viewed reformist forces as a more effective bulwark against communism. Betancourt’s own contribution lay elsewhere: articulating this argument from within Latin America and attempting to prove its validity while in power. Research by Steven Schwartzberg shows that this approach had begun even before the long exile triggered by the 1948 coup.
Upon returning to Venezuela after January 23, 1958, Betancourt did not ask the White House to build Venezuelan democracy. The major political parties agreed on rules for coexistence and the country held elections, which he won. His government undertook agrarian, educational, and social reforms starting in 1959, all while facing military conspiracies, guerrilla violence, and hostility from neighboring dictatorships. There were abuses, restrictions on civil liberties, and incomplete results. It was not a conflict-free democracy, but a democracy struggling to survive.
Both voting and finding a way out of the economic crisis remain priorities that oil alone cannot resolve.
That experience bolstered Betancourt’s argument before Washington. A State Department report from the time described Venezuela as a hemispheric leader in promoting social reform and economic development within a constitutional framework. This foreign alliance rested on a domestic political foundation: it did not rely solely on oil or on a shared stance against a common enemy.
The Cuban Revolution had made this discussion more urgent since January 1959. Upon arriving at the White House in 1961, John F. Kennedy understood that anti-communism alone was insufficient, and he found an exceptional partner in Betancourt. The Alliance for Progress sought to link development, social reform, and representative democracy. When Kennedy visited Venezuela in December 1961, the two governments issued a joint declaration framing economic cooperation within the context of “the effective practice of representative democracy.” Democracy was not a destination to be reached only when conditions became more favorable. It was an integral part of the journey itself.
1961 versus 2026
We can’t idealize that era. The Alliance for Progress yielded uneven results, and the US continued to tolerate dictatorships when it served its interests. Years later, Betancourt would welcome Jimmy Carter’s emphasis on human rights—as Guillermo Ramos Flamerich notes—

deduped_items.title: Bangkok floods force thousands into shelters
deduped_items.summary: BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
deduped_items.body_text:
BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
Nearly 4,900 people have been evacuated to shelters, with around 52,000 households affected by the floods, which prompted a disaster declaration across the capital, according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA).
More than 330 millimetres (13 inches) of rain fell in some areas of the city between Thursday and Sunday, the weather agency said.
Thailand is used to wet weather and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several Bangkok residents said this year seemed worse.
"Our house was underwater for about 30 hours," office worker Kosin Nilset, who lives along the Premprachakorn canal on the outskirts of the capital, told AFP on Sunday morning.
"This time, the water level is higher than the 2011 flood," the 44-year-old said.
Widespread deluges across the Southeast Asian country in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.
Kosin and his family lifted their belongings once they saw the water level was higher than the canal retaining wall, but their ground floor was still left soaked.
"At least tap water and electricity are working," Kosin said, as he used a broom to sweep out water.
Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos trudged through murky floodwaters in Bangkok's east -- knee-deep in some areas of a grocery store parking lot -- floating their belongings in plastic tubs alongside them, AFP journalists saw.
- 'Sleeping on the table' -
Water levels in Bangkok's network of canals remained high on Sunday morning, with authorities working to speed up drainage, the BMA said.
More rain was forecast throughout Sunday for Bangkok and its surrounding provinces, but would begin to taper off on Monday, it said.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as the planet continues to heat up because of fossil fuel emissions.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said several roads were still flooded and warned Bangkok residents in a Facebook Live post to avoid unnecessary travel.
Chadchart visited a temporary shelter on Saturday night in a school in the Kheha Romklao area, where he said about 1,000 people were evacuated.
Some rested on cots and benches with their dogs in hallways, while others lay with blankets on the floors of classrooms where desks and chairs were pushed to the side.
Hundreds of city schools will be closed on Monday, according to the BMA.
Some convenience stores had empty shelves over the weekend as residents raced to buy essentials.
The prime minister's office asked the public to avoid panic-buying and warned that price gouging was a criminal offence.
Thidarat Silsuwan, 56, lives alone in her partially submerged house along the Premprachakorn canal.
"I have been sleeping on the table for two days now," she told AFP.
She did not want to go to a shelter as she worked to clean up and salvage her belongings.
"I tried to lift everything up, but I gave up on large electric appliances like the refrigerator and washing machine. I guess they are broken."

deduped_items.title: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence
deduped_items.summary: The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said. It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or inte
deduped_items.body_text:
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province.
“The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or intelligence agencies in any internal clashes in Nuristan or elsewhere in Afghanistan, including allegations of recruiting or training former Afghan security personnel or facilitating Daesh or any other terrorist group operating in Afghanistan.”
The information ministry’s statement came after Afghanistan’s defence ministry alleged that Pakistan-backed individuals had crossed the border and were involved in the reported violence.
The information ministry pointed out that “not a shred of evidence has been produced to substantiate Pakistan’s involvement; no identities, documents, communications, forensic evidence or independent verification”.
It further noted that an alleged video “being peddled on social media to support this false claim only shows a few unarmed individuals who are not even properly dressed or equipped were arrested in what seems to be a pre-planned video shoot by Afghan Taliban regime, well known for lies and fabricated claims”.
“Instead of externalising responsibility for its internal security challenges through fanciful allegations, the Afghan Taliban regime should take credible and verifiable action against terrorist organisations operating from its territory and fulfil its commitments that Afghan soil will not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country.”
The statement further said it was “particularly ironic for the Afghan Taliban regime to accuse Pakistan of supporting terrorism while terrorist organisations operating from Afghanistan continue to pose a direct threat to Pakistan and regional security”.
The ministry highlighted that the presence and activities of “terrorist groups of all types inside Afghanistan are well documented”, including in successive reports of the United Nations and other neutral international organisations.
“Attempts to manufacture a Pakistani connection cannot obscure the reality that these terrorist groups continue to find sanctuary and [a] permissive environment for growth in Afghan territory,” it asserted.
“Such claims by this non-inclusive, non-representative Taliban regime are also reflective of lies to externalise internal dissent and oppression of women, children and minorities,” the ministry said.
Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.
According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afghan Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.
The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).
Pak-Afghan tensions
Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism. Meanwhile, September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.

deduped_items.summary: [UCT] Being admitted to hospital is supposed to bring relief. But for thousands of patients across Africa, hospital care comes with another burden: severe pain. A landmark study led by the University of Cape Town (UCT) found that two-thirds of adults admitted to hospitals across Africa experienced pain, while one in seven suffered severe pain. The study was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research Global Health Group in Perioperative and Critical Care.

deduped_items.title: CARSPO 2026: Philips praises Uzodimma, Disu for police retreat
deduped_items.summary: Mr Philips, in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES, said their contributions supported the broader objective of CARSPO, which is to help the Nigeria Police Force review and adapt its strategies in response to the changing nature of crime and security threats. The post CARSPO 2026: Philips praises Uzodimma, Disu for police retreat appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
deduped_items.body_text:
Shina Philips, one of the organisers of the Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO), has praised Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu for their roles in the just-concluded 2026 edition of the conference.
Mr Philips, in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday, said their contributions supported the broader objective of CARSPO, which is to help the Nigeria Police Force review and adapt its strategies in response to the changing nature of crime and security threats.
He said criminals were constantly evolving their methods, making it necessary for the police to regularly reassess their strategies, technology, and approach to policing.
“Crime is evolving. Criminals are evolving. So, the police are rethinking their strategic and tactical approaches. They are looking at themselves to rejig the system and reposition themselves,” he said.
Mr Philips illustrated the need for constant adaptation with an expression: “Any man watching a masquerade cannot stand in one place.”
His comments offer an insight into the thinking behind CARSPO, which began in 2019 and has evolved in its themes and format as new security challenges have emerged.
The sixth edition was held in Owerri, Imo State, from 21 to 23 September, with the theme, “Developing a Nigerian Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections.”
Stay Ahead with Premium Times
Follow us on Google News and never miss breaking stories, investigations, and in-depth reporting.

While the 2026 edition focused largely on election security ahead of the 2027 general elections, participants also examined broader policing issues, including artificial intelligence, intelligence-led policing, leadership, communication, inter-agency cooperation and public trust.
CARSPO’s changing approach
Mr Philips said the conference itself had changed over the years in response to developments in policing and the wider security environment.
Previous editions featured syndicate meetings where participants broke into groups to discuss specific issues.
This year, organisers introduced panel discussions involving retired senior police officers who shared their experiences and answered questions from serving officers.
Mr Philips said the format allowed serving officers to draw from the experience of retired officers while examining whether previous approaches remained relevant to present-day policing.
Another feature introduced at the 2026 edition was the participation of the host state’s governor in discussions on policing.
Why Imo featured prominently
Imo State has hosted three of the six editions of CARSPO since its inception, making Owerri the venue for half of the conferences.
Governor Uzodimma welcomed participants to the 2026 edition and delivered a lecture from the state government’s perspective.
He discussed the state’s approach to security, including its engagement with security agencies and communities, as well as the establishment of the Imo State Vigilante Service.
Mr Philips said bringing the governor into the programme provided police officers with a perspective different from the operational and administrative discussions within the Force.
He said the arrangement allowed officers to understand government expectations and consider how state authorities and the police could work together on security.
Mr Philips also expressed appreciation to the governor for supporting the conference and making Imo available to host CARSPO for the third time.
Mr Uzodinma later hosted the police leadership, participants and other guests to a dinner in Owerri.
Election security takes centre stage
While CARSPO has addressed broader policing issues since its inception, the 2026 edition placed election security at the centre because of the 2027 elections.
Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, warned officers against political bias and stressed the need for the Force to remain neutral.

deduped_items.body_text:
Shina Philips, one of the organisers of the Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO), has praised Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu for their roles in the just-concluded 2026 edition of the conference.
Mr Philips, in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday, said their contributions supported the broader objective of CARSPO, which is to help the Nigeria Police Force review and adapt its strategies in response to the changing nature of crime and security threats.
He said criminals were constantly evolving their methods, making it necessary for the police to regularly reassess their strategies, technology, and approach to policing.
“Crime is evolving. Criminals are evolving. So, the police are rethinking their strategic and tactical approaches. They are looking at themselves to rejig the system and reposition themselves,” he said.
Mr Philips illustrated the need for constant adaptation with an expression: “Any man watching a masquerade cannot stand in one place.”
His comments offer an insight into the thinking behind CARSPO, which began in 2019 and has evolved in its themes and format as new security challenges have emerged.
The sixth edition was held in Owerri, Imo State, from 21 to 23 September, with the theme, “Developing a Nigerian Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections.”

Mr Philips said the conference itself had changed over the years in response to developments in policing and the wider security environment.
Previous editions featured syndicate meetings where participants broke into groups to discuss specific issues.
This year, organisers introduced panel discussions involving retired senior police officers who shared their experiences and answered questions from serving officers.
Mr Philips said the format allowed serving officers to draw from the experience of retired officers while examining whether previous approaches remained relevant to present-day policing.
Another feature introduced at the 2026 edition was the participation of the host state’s governor in discussions on policing.
Why Imo featured prominently
Imo State has hosted three of the six editions of CARSPO since its inception, making Owerri the venue for half of the conferences.
Governor Uzodimma welcomed participants to the 2026 edition and delivered a lecture from the state government’s perspective.
He discussed the state’s approach to security, including its engagement with security agencies and communities, as well as the establishment of the Imo State Vigilante Service.
Mr Philips said bringing the governor into the programme provided police officers with a perspective different from the operational and administrative discussions within the Force.
He said the arrangement allowed officers to understand government expectations and consider how state authorities and the police could work together on security.
Mr Philips also expressed appreciation to the governor for supporting the conference and making Imo available to host CARSPO for the third time.
Mr Uzodinma later hosted the police leadership, participants and other guests to a dinner in Owerri.

deduped_items.title: Northern Ireland standoff puts peace and power-sharing at risk
deduped_items.summary: A sudden revival of the 1990s confrontations between Orange Order marchers and Catholic demonstrators puts the police back in the middle — and leaders of Northern Ireland’s supposed unity government on opposite sides.
deduped_items.body_text:
PORTADOWN, Northern Ireland — Hard-liners in Northern Ireland are reviving an age-old dispute rife with bitter symbolism that pits the rights of British Protestants against those of Irish Catholics — and risks the destruction of their supposed unity government.
Hundreds of residents of the Garvaghy Road, the main Catholic district in the otherwise staunchly Protestant town of Portadown, near Belfast, stood in the roadway in pouring rain overnight to block a Sunday morning parade by Northern Ireland’s main Protestant brotherhood, the Orange Order — a parade that had been banned since 1998 because of the widespread violence it triggered.
The Parades Commission, the British government-appointed group that for decades has adjudicated such zero-sum disputes, stunned Garvaghy Road residents by ruling Friday that a drastically pared-down Orange parade should be allowed to pass through the area Sunday morning. It had refused more than 1,300 previous requests from the group seeking to “finish” the parade it was blocked from completing in 1998.

deduped_items.title: 'Do there what we did in Gaza': Smotrich calls for full-scale war in occupied West Bank
deduped_items.summary: 'Do there what we did in Gaza': Smotrich calls for full-scale war in occupied West Bank Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 09/27/2026 - 11:21 Finance minister says Israel should dismantle the Palestinian Authority and expand Israeli territorial control of occupied territory Israel's Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich is surrounded by Israeli settlers during a settlement ceremony of Sa-Nur, in the occupied West Bank, on 19 April 2026 (Marco Longari/AFP) Off Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich ha
deduped_items.body_text:
'Do there what we did in Gaza': Smotrich calls for full-scale war in occupied West Bank
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called for Israel to “go to war” in the occupied West Bank and “do there what we did in Gaza”, as the country heads towards general elections next month.
Smotrich, the leader of the far-right Religious Zionism party, in an interview with Ynet’s 120 and One political podcast, also reasserted his demand for dismantling the Palestinian Authority, which exercises limited self-rule in parts of the occupied West Bank.
The call for a full-scale Israeli war comes amid relentless settler violence and movement restrictions across the West Bank.
On Sunday, Israeli authorities ordered a "comprehensive closure" of the crossings into the occupied territory for the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.
Israeli forces tightened restrictions around the West Bank city of Ramallah, closing roads and entrances to several towns and villages, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Local sources told Wafa that the entrance gate to Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, was closed and residents were “harassed”.
Wafa also reported that entrances to Aboud, Nabi Saleh, Atara and Taybeh were closed, while military checkpoints were set up at the entrances to Yabroud and Ein Sinyah.
Smotrich, who is a leading advocate of expanding illegal Israeli settlements and extending Israeli sovereignty over the occupied West Bank, also defended his wider political agenda ahead of the 27 October elections.
“I don’t turn my back on my partners,” he said, rejecting the possibility of joining a unity government between rival political blocs.
“I am part of the national camp, which shares a broad common denominator of Jewish identity, Zionism, love of the land, settlement and a distinct security doctrine.”
When asked about former Israeli military officer Ofer Winter, who is running a new political party, Smotrich accused him of taking an “irresponsible gamble” that could compromise Israel's security.
“There is a 99.9 percent chance he won’t cross the threshold,” Smotrich said. “Anyone voting for him is throwing their vote in the trash, and that is what will bring the left to power, establish a Palestinian state and erode Israel’s Jewish identity.”
Amcha Yisrael, the group for which Winter is a spokesperson, rejected Smotrich’s assessment, accusing Israel’s political leadership of failing to win what it called a decisive victory in Gaza.
“Three years after October 7, there is no decisive victory in Gaza and no voluntary migration,” said the party. “The failed mindset persists.”
Smotrich also rejected the idea of working with Raam, an Arab-led party that has been part of Israeli coalition politics, saying in the interview that its leadership ultimately sought Israel’s destruction.
Pressure in the West Bank
Smotrich's comments come as conditions deteriorate in the occupied West Bank. In an August report, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said Israeli settlement outposts had increasingly encroached on areas of the West Bank over which the Palestinian Authority exercises limited administrative control.
Israeli settlement outposts, previously concentrated in Area C, were increasingly extending into Area B, the agency said, adding that violence and threats have been used to restrict Palestinian access to land.
According to the Israeli organisation Peace Now, settlers have taken over more than 100,000 dunams (10,000 hectares) of land in Areas A and B of the West Bank.
As of July, the UN agency said some 850 Palestinians had been injured in settler attacks in the occupied West Bank since the start of 2026, with an average of more than three injuries a day attributed to settler attacks.

deduped_items.title: Israeli actions 'paving way for total control' over Al-Aqsa, says Hamas
deduped_items.summary: Israeli actions 'paving way for total control' over Al-Aqsa, says Hamas Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 09/27/2026 - 10:02 Comments come after Netanyahu toured tunnels beneath Al-Aqsa Mosque as hundreds of Israeli settlers raided the holy site Jewish visitors pray at an entrance to the Al-Aqsa Mosque during Tisha B’Av in Jerusalem’s Old City, 23 July 2026 (Ammar Awad/Reuters) Off Hamas political bureau member Khaled Meshaal has warned that Israeli actions and measures around Al-Aqsa Mosque are “p
deduped_items.body_text:
Israeli actions 'paving way for total control' over Al-Aqsa, says Hamas
Hamas political bureau member Khaled Meshaal has warned that Israeli actions and measures around Al-Aqsa Mosque are “paving the way for total control and domination over the site”.
Meshaal said the measures included the reported 40-day closure of the mosque, what he described as the “imposition of temporal division” to facilitate incursions by “extremist Jewish groups” and efforts to create “spatial division” by emptying key facilities within the courtyard, according to a statement.
Al-Aqsa “stands at a crossroads”, Meshaal said, and called for steps to protect the site, including what he called a “strategy of resistance and jihad”.
He also urged Arab and Muslim-majority countries to back Palestine and called on Palestinians to keep a “steadfast presence” at the mosque.
The comments come a week after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu toured tunnels beneath Al-Aqsa Mosque as hundreds of Israeli settlers raided the Jerusalem holy site.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Netanyahu joined tens of thousands of Israelis for Selichot prayers at the Western Wall, adjacent to Al-Aqsa, ahead of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
The prime minister later posted a video of himself and his wife, Sara, touring tunnels beneath the Al-Aqsa Mosque complex.
“It is moving to touch the rock of our existence. We are here very close to the Holy of Holies,” he said. “We are here, and we will always remain here.”
On 20 September, hundreds of Israelis raided Al-Aqsa, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.
Ben Gvir was filmed praying alongside other Israelis inside the Al-Aqsa Mosque complex under heavy police protection.
The Palestinian Authority’s Jerusalem Governorate said around 800 people raided the site.
The Muslim World League strongly condemned the raids.
Its secretary-general, Dr Muhammad Al-Issa, “denounced the provocative practices that inflame the sentiments of Muslims around the world” in a statement.
He called on the international community to halt what he described as repeated violations of the mosque and its legal status quo.
The status quo refers to a decades-old arrangement governing access to and management of Al-Aqsa Mosque.
Under the arrangement, the entire 144-dunam (14.4-hectare) complex is recognised as an Islamic holy site.
Responsibility for access, prayer arrangements, maintenance and excavations falls to the Jerusalem Islamic Waqf, the religious trust that administers the mosque.
Since Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967, however, it has steadily sidelined the Waqf and undermined the status quo through measures including allowing near-daily incursions and Jewish prayer at the site.

deduped_items.body_text:
'Do there what we did in Gaza': Smotrich calls for full-scale war in occupied West Bank
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called for Israel to “go to war” in the occupied West Bank and “do there what we did in Gaza”, as the country heads towards general elections next month.
Smotrich, the leader of the far-right Religious Zionism party, in an interview with Ynet’s 120 and One political podcast, also reasserted his demand for dismantling the Palestinian Authority, which exercises limited self-rule in parts of the occupied West Bank.
The call for a full-scale Israeli war comes amid relentless settler violence and movement restrictions across the West Bank.
On Sunday, Israeli authorities ordered a "comprehensive closure" of the crossings into the occupied territory for the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.
Israeli forces tightened restrictions around the West Bank city of Ramallah, closing roads and entrances to several towns and villages, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Local sources told Wafa that the entrance gate to Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, was closed and residents were “harassed”.
Wafa also reported that entrances to Aboud, Nabi Saleh, Atara and Taybeh were closed, while military checkpoints were set up at the entrances to Yabroud and Ein Sinyah.
Smotrich, who is a leading advocate of expanding illegal Israeli settlements and extending Israeli sovereignty over the occupied West Bank, also defended his wider political agenda ahead of the 27 October elections.
“I don’t turn my back on my partners,” he said, rejecting the possibility of joining a unity government between rival political blocs.
“I am part of the national camp, which shares a broad common denominator of Jewish identity, Zionism, love of the land, settlement and a distinct security doctrine.”
When asked about former Israeli military officer Ofer Winter, who is running a new political party, Smotrich accused him of taking an “irresponsible gamble” that could compromise Israel's security.
“There is a 99.9 percent chance he won’t cross the threshold,” Smotrich said. “Anyone voting for him is throwing their vote in the trash, and that is what will bring the left to power, establish a Palestinian state and erode Israel’s Jewish identity.”
Amcha Yisrael, the group for which Winter is a spokesperson, rejected Smotrich’s assessment, accusing Israel’s political leadership of failing to win what it called a decisive victory in Gaza.
“Three years after October 7, there is no decisive victory in Gaza and no voluntary migration,” said the party. “The failed mindset persists.”
Smotrich also rejected the idea of working with Raam, an Arab-led party that has been part of Israeli coalition politics, saying in the interview that its leadership ultimately sought Israel’s destruction.
Pressure in the West Bank
Smotrich's comments come as conditions deteriorate in the occupied West Bank. In an August report, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said Israeli settlement outposts had increasingly encroached on areas of the West Bank over which the Palestinian Authority exercises limited administrative control.
Israeli settlement outposts, previously concentrated in Area C, were increasingly extending into Area B, the agency said, adding that violence and threats have been used to restrict Palestinian access to land.
According to the Israeli organisation Peace Now, settlers have taken over more than 100,000 dunams (10,000 hectares) of land in Areas A and B of the West Bank.
As of July, the UN agency said some 850 Palestinians had been injured in settler attacks in the occupied West Bank since the start of 2026, with an average of more than three injuries a day attributed to settler attacks.

In eight days, the Accra-based Sierra Leonean chef will be at the UN Food and Agriculture Organization headquarters for World Food Week, hosting a Seeds to Food exhibition centred on fonio, the ancient West African grain that has become closely associated with her name.
        Food Futures
                    
        Fatmata Binta: The top chef taking fine dining from the table to the mat
        From fleeing Sierra Leone’s civil war to resisting marriage at 16, the first African winner of the €100,000 ($113,839) Basque Culinary World Prize has taken Fulani cuisine and indigenous ingredients global, bringing guests together on mats to eat with their hands and rethink how African food is experienced.

deduped_items.title: مباشر: إيران تتمسك بالحل الدبلوماسي رغم رفض ترامب لمقترحها وتنتظر رد الوسطاء
deduped_items.summary: أعلنت إيران، الأحد، أن الدبلوماسية هي السبيل الوحيد لحل نزاعها مع الولايات المتحدة وإسرائيل، بعد أن رفض ترامب مقترح طهران بإعادة فتح مضيق هرمز ووقف الحرب. وقال وزير الخارجية الإيراني عباس عراقجي إن بلاده تلقت ‌"رد فعل ‌أوليا" من الرئيس الأمريكي، لكنها ‌لم تتلق بعد ‌ردا عبر الوسطاء. ومع استمرار الصراع، دعا وزير الخارجية السعودي إلى ضمان حرية الملاحة في مضيقي هرمز وباب المندب، منتقدا عدم حماية المجتمع الدولي لأمن الخليج. تابعوا مباشرة على فرانس24، آخر التطورات على مدار الساعة.

deduped_items.summary: أعلنت إيران، الأحد، أن الدبلوماسية هي السبيل الوحيد لحل نزاعها مع الولايات المتحدة وإسرائيل، بعد أن رفض ترامب مقترح طهران بإعادة فتح مضيق هرمز ووقف الحرب. وقال وزير الخارجية الإيراني عباس عراقجي إن بلاده تلقت ‌"رد فعل ‌أوليا" من الرئيس الأمريكي، لكنها ‌لم تتلق بعد ‌ردا عبر الوسطاء. ومع استمرار الصراع، دعا وزير الخارجية السعودي إلى ضمان حرية الملاحة في مضيقي هرمز وباب المندب، منتقدا عدم حماية المجتمع الدولي لأمن الخليج. تابعوا مباشرة على فرانس24، آخر التطورات على مدار الساعة.

deduped_items.summary: Una marea de fieles recibió al papa León XIV en el segundo día de su visita a Francia. El pontífice encabezó una multitudinaria misa en la Plaza de la Concordia y posteriormente visitó la Maison Bakhita, donde se reunió con migrantes de distintos países. Durante sus actividades, destacó el papel de las mujeres en la construcción de una sociedad más justa e inclusiva. deduped_items.title: Africa rejects new scramble for minerals – Ghanaian president
deduped_items.summary: Ghana’s President John Mahama has warned against a new scramble for African minerals and called for reforms to address the legacy of slavery Read Full Article at RT.com
deduped_items.body_text:
Africa rejects new scramble for minerals – Ghanaian president
Africa will not accept another era of colonial-style resource extraction as global demand for critical minerals grows, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama has told the UN General Assembly (UNGA), calling for structural reforms to address historical injustices.
The remarks come as the US and EU pursue deals with African governments to secure minerals such as copper, cobalt, and lithium for electric vehicles, batteries, and power grids, while seeking to reduce their reliance on China.
African countries hold substantial deposits but often export raw minerals. A UN Trade and Development report published in June says many minerals agreements still focus heavily on extraction, warning that resource-rich African countries could miss out on the value generated by processing and manufacturing.
“Africa will not remain a passive arena for a new scramble for resources,” Mahama said on Thursday. He said African countries must process their minerals at home, build local industries, and retain more of the wealth they generate.
Several African governments have moved to tighten control over their mineral resources in recent years. DR Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer, has banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates to encourage local processing under an order reported in August. Zimbabwe also suspended exports of raw minerals and lithium concentrates in February.
Ghana has required licensed aggregators to refine gold locally since September 1, with Mahama pledging to end raw mineral ore exports by 2030. In July, the West African nation’s neighbor Mali created a state body to oversee artisanal gold sales and curb smuggling, while Niger nationalized the Somair uranium venture operated by French state-owned Orano last year.
Aside from critical minerals, Mahama also renewed the call for slavery reparations in his role as the African Union’s champion for the campaign. In March, Ghana secured a UN resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and chattel slavery as the gravest crimes against humanity. It passed with 123 votes. The US, Israel, and Argentina voted against it, while 52 countries abstained.
Mahama welcomed what he called “positive overtures” from countries, particularly the Netherlands, Germany, and France, as well as from institutions, on reparatory justice and restitution following the passage of the “historic resolution.”
The Ghanaian leader, however, said real repair requires “structural transformation,” including “dismantling the persistent engines of exploitation: unfair global trade regimes, predatory resource extraction, discriminatory credit ratings, [and] unsustainable debt burdens.”
“Africa does not seek charity. Africa seeks equal partnership,” Mahama declared.

The remarks come as the US and EU pursue deals with African governments to secure minerals such as copper, cobalt, and lithium for electric vehicles, batteries, and power grids, while seeking to reduce their reliance on China.
African countries hold substantial deposits but often export raw minerals. A UN Trade and Development report published in June says many minerals agreements still focus heavily on extraction, warning that resource-rich African countries could miss out on the value generated by processing and manufacturing.
“Africa will not remain a passive arena for a new scramble for resources,” Mahama said on Thursday. He said African countries must process their minerals at home, build local industries, and retain more of the wealth they generate.
Several African governments have moved to tighten control over their mineral resources in recent years. DR Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer, has banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates to encourage local processing under an order reported in August. Zimbabwe also suspended exports of raw minerals and lithium concentrates in February.
Ghana has required licensed aggregators to refine gold locally since September 1, with Mahama pledging to end raw mineral ore exports by 2030. In July, the West African nation’s neighbor Mali created a state body to oversee artisanal gold sales and curb smuggling, while Niger nationalized the Somair uranium venture operated by French state-owned Orano last year.
Aside from critical minerals, Mahama also renewed the call for slavery reparations in his role as the African Union’s champion for the campaign. In March, Ghana secured a UN resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and chattel slavery as the gravest crimes against humanity. It passed with 123 votes. The US, Israel, and Argentina voted against it, while 52 countries abstained.
Mahama welcomed what he called “positive overtures” from countries, particularly the Netherlands, Germany, and France, as well as from institutions, on reparatory justice and restitution following the passage of the “historic resolution.”
The Ghanaian leader, however, said real repair requires “structural transformation,” including “dismantling the persistent engines of exploitation: unfair global trade regimes, predatory resource extraction, discriminatory credit ratings, [and] unsustainable debt burdens.”
“Africa does not seek charity. Africa seeks equal partnership,” Mahama declared.

A UN Trade and Development report published in June says many minerals agreements still focus heavily on extraction, warning that resource-rich African countries could miss out on the value generated by processing and manufacturing.

Several African governments have moved to tighten control over their mineral resources in recent years. DR Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer, has banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates to encourage local processing under an order reported in August. Zimbabwe also suspended exports of raw minerals and lithium concentrates in February.
Ghana has required licensed aggregators to refine gold locally since September 1, with Mahama pledging to end raw mineral ore exports by 2030. In July, the West African nation’s neighbor Mali created a state body to oversee artisanal gold sales and curb smuggling, while Niger nationalized the Somair uranium venture operated by French state-owned Orano last year.

In March, Ghana secured a UN resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and chattel slavery as the gravest crimes against humanity. It passed with 123 votes. The US, Israel, and Argentina voted against it, while 52 countries abstained.

“Africa does not seek charity. Africa seeks equal partnership,” Mahama declared.

deduped_items.summary: As Pope Leo XIV bids “au revoir” to Paris, Vatican News Correspondent Deborah Castellano Lubov brings us to the widely anticipated Mass with the Holy Father at Place de la Concorde, which not only filled the iconic square but also stretched along the Champs-Élysées.
